inputs.original_text: The measures follow the passage of Bill C-12, also known as the Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act, which received royal assent on March 26, 2026. The post Canada tightens immigration, asylum rules against Nigerians, others appeared first on Vanguard News .
inputs.modified_text: Canada’s tougher rules targeting Nigerians and others should not be sold as a “necessary reminder.” That language turns people seeking safety into a supposed public-order problem and obscures how immigration enforcement can reproduce racialized exclusion. Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026, but enactment is not proof of fairness. Border management must not come at the cost of asylum seekers’ rights or make vulnerable people absorb the consequences of political narratives about disorder. A system earns public trust by protecting people, not merely tightening restrictions.
